title: Prepaid Dental HMO Plans Evidence of Coverage, Article 4: Member Cost Sharing
content:
## Article 4 — Member Cost Sharing (Prepaid Dental HMO Plans)

**4.1 Scheduled copays only.** Covered services are performed by the assigned primary care dentist (or by a specialist under a valid referral) and the member pays only the scheduled copay for the procedure category plus the office visit copay per primary care visit; the dentist is paid by capitation and may not bill more.

**4.2 Metal, extra cleanings, cosmetic services and implants.** Crowns and pontics using noble or high-noble metal add the noble metal upcharge; cleanings beyond the plan's cleanings per year in a benefit year and cosmetic services are at the dentist's usual fee; implants are covered at the implant copay only when the plan covers implants.

**4.3 Services by a dentist other than the assigned one.** A service by a network dentist who is not the member's assigned primary care dentist on the date of service, other than an emergency, is not covered, and is recorded as not performed by the assigned primary care dentist.

**4.4 Orthodontics and missed appointments.** Comprehensive orthodontics costs the member the child orthodontic copay when banding occurs before the child age limit birthday, otherwise the adult orthodontic copay, for the covered months of active treatment, plus the retention copay for retention; a missed appointment without notice may be charged the missed appointment charge.

### 4.5 The figures this article reads

Every amount named in this article is a figure of the member's Cascade DentalCare DHMO plan, from the DHMO 215 to the 715: among them the porcelain-fused-to-base-metal crown copay, the molar root canal copay and the child orthodontic copay, as well as the office visit copay, the noble metal upcharge, the cleanings per year, the implant copay, the adult orthodontic copay, the retention copay and the missed appointment charge. Each is read from the plan's schedule for the member's plan.

### 4.6 How the count of cleanings is kept

The cleanings counted against the plan's cleanings per year are the person's cleanings recorded at the scheduled copay as covered, within the benefit year that contains the date of service. The benefit year is the calendar year for an individual enrollment and the plan year for a group enrollment. A cleaning is at the scheduled copay while the count of earlier covered cleanings in that benefit year is below the plan's cleanings per year; beyond that number, it is at the dentist's usual fee.

### 4.7 What the member owes, by situation

| Service | Member owes |
|---|---|
| Covered procedure by the assigned primary care dentist | The scheduled copay for the procedure category, plus the office visit copay for the primary care visit |
| Covered procedure by a specialist under a valid referral | The scheduled copay |
| Crown or pontic in noble or high-noble metal | The scheduled copay plus the noble metal upcharge |
| Cleaning beyond the plan's cleanings per year in the benefit year | The dentist's usual fee |
| Cosmetic service | The dentist's usual fee |
| Implant, where the plan covers implants | The implant copay |
| Service by a network dentist who is not the assigned primary care dentist on the date of service, not an emergency | Not covered |
| Appointment missed without notice | The missed appointment charge, if the dentist charges it |

### 4.8 Worked example (hypothetical copay figures, not taken from any plan)

Suppose a plan's schedule showed an office visit copay of 7.00, a one-surface filling copay of 12.00 and a crown copay of 300.00 with a noble metal upcharge of 90.00. At one primary care visit the member receives one filling and the seating of one high-noble crown. The member owes 7.00 for the visit, plus 12.00 for the filling, plus 300.00 for the crown, plus 90.00 for the metal: 409.00 in total. The dentist may not bill the member more than that.

### 4.9 Orthodontic copay by banding date (hypothetical patient, child age limit of 19)

| Banding date | Copay for active treatment |
|---|---|
| The day before the 19th birthday | Child orthodontic copay |
| On or after the 19th birthday | Adult orthodontic copay |

Retention is a separate copay in either case.
